subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Gestational Hypertension, Pre-eclampsia, Eclampsia and HELLP

steps.tx: New blood pressure elevation after twenty weeks without proteinuria or organ features is **gestational hypertension**. Many cases progress to pre-eclampsia, so surveillance is close. It resolves by twelve weeks after delivery by definition. Up to half develop pre-eclampsia within one to three weeks, the figure that justifies twice weekly checks.
steps.say: Gestational hypertension rises after twenty weeks without organ features and needs close surveillance.

steps.tx: Hypertension with proteinuria or maternal organ dysfunction after twenty weeks defines **preeclampsia** in modern spelling pre-eclampsia. Placental disease drives widespread endothelial dysfunction in the mother. Delivery of the placenta remains the only cure. Proteinuria is no longer compulsory for diagnosis when platelets, liver, kidney or brain features appear.
steps.say: Pre-eclampsia combines hypertension with proteinuria or organ dysfunction and delivery cures it.

steps.tx: Features marking dangerous disease include severe headache, visual disturbance, epigastric pain and very high pressure, grouped as **severe features**. Any one mandates urgent hospital assessment and delivery planning. Blood pressure of one sixty over one ten is itself a severe feature. Blood pressure at or above 160 over 110 needs treatment within 30 to 60 minutes to prevent maternal stroke.
steps.say: Severe features like headache, visual change and epigastric pain mandate urgent delivery planning.

steps.tx: Generalised convulsions in a woman with pre-eclampsia, not explained otherwise, define **eclampsia**. Most fits are brief and self limiting, but maternal hypoxia endangers both lives. Magnesium sulphate prevents and treats these seizures. Most fits last one to two minutes, and only about one in ten women who fit has no prior documented hypertension.
steps.say: Eclampsia convulses women with pre-eclampsia and magnesium sulphate treats the seizures.

steps.tx: Haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets together form **HELLP syndrome**. It complicates severe pre-eclampsia and can occur without very high pressure. Epigastric pain with malaise in late pregnancy should always trigger its exclusion. HELLP can present after delivery, and right upper quadrant pain with nausea is its commonest calling card.
steps.say: HELLP syndrome combines haemolysis, raised liver enzymes and low platelets in severe disease.

steps.tx: Failed spiral artery remodelling in early pregnancy starts the disease, a process of **defective placentation**. The ischaemic placenta releases antiangiogenic factors into maternal blood. These injure endothelium everywhere, explaining the multisystem picture. Soluble Flt1 rises and placental growth factor falls weeks before symptoms, the imbalance behind newer blood tests.
steps.say: Defective placentation releases antiangiogenic factors that injure maternal endothelium everywhere.

steps.tx: Low dose aspirin started before sixteen weeks prevents pre-eclampsia in high risk women, termed **aspirin prophylaxis**. Previous pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension and diabetes qualify. It is taken at night until about thirty six weeks. Aspirin started after 16 weeks loses most benefit, so the first dose belongs in the late first trimester.
steps.say: Aspirin prophylaxis before sixteen weeks prevents pre-eclampsia in high risk women.

steps.tx: Calcium supplementation prevents disease where dietary intake is low, an intervention of **calcium prophylaxis**. One to two grams daily from mid pregnancy is the studied dose. It complements rather than replaces aspirin in high risk women. It works best in populations eating under 600 milligrams of calcium a day, common in low income diets.
steps.say: Calcium prophylaxis prevents pre-eclampsia where dietary intake is low.

steps.tx: After delivery, hypertension may worsen before improving over days, called **postpartum evolution**. A quarter of eclampsia occurs after birth, so vigilance continues on postnatal wards. Persistent hypertension beyond twelve weeks reclassifies as chronic. Blood pressure peaks around day three to five after birth, so discharge on day one needs a planned early review.
steps.say: Postpartum evolution can worsen hypertension after delivery, with a quarter of eclampsia postnatal.
